files: /etc/cron.weekly/fstrim
/etc/sysctl.d/80-installer-tuning.conf

# System tuning, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings. Delete this file to go back to the kernel's values.
# A leading "-" lets a kernel without the setting skip it (systemd-sysctl and procps sysctl both read it so).
# Keep more of the directory and file-name cache in memory.
vm.vfs_cache_pressure = 50
# Write changed data to disk early and in smaller amounts, so a large copy does not stall the desktop.
vm.dirty_bytes = 268435456
vm.dirty_background_bytes = 67108864
vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs = 1500
# A longer queue for received network packets.
-net.core.netdev_max_backlog = 4096
# The NMI watchdog costs CPU time and power, and a desktop or laptop does not need it.
-kernel.nmi_watchdog = 0
/etc/udev/rules.d/60-installer-ioschedulers.rules

# I/O schedulers by disk type, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings. Delete this file to use the kernel's choice.
# Hard disks: BFQ keeps the desktop responsive while the disk is busy.
ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="block", KERNEL=="sd[a-z]*", ATTR{queue/rotational}=="1", ATTR{queue/scheduler}="bfq"
# SATA SSDs, SD and eMMC cards: mq-deadline.
ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="block", KERNEL=="sd[a-z]*|mmcblk[0-9]*", ATTR{queue/rotational}=="0", ATTR{queue/scheduler}="mq-deadline"
# NVMe SSDs: Kyber, which keeps reads quick while much is written.
ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="block", KERNEL=="nvme[0-9]*n[0-9]*", ATTR{queue/rotational}=="0", ATTR{queue/scheduler}="kyber"
/etc/tmpfiles.d/installer-thp.conf

# Transparent huge pages, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings. Delete this file to use the kernel's values.
# A program that asks for huge pages gets them without waiting for memory to be compacted.
w! /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag - - - - defer+madvise
# Split a huge page again when most of it (80 percent) is unused, so that memory is not wasted.
w! /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/khugepaged/max_ptes_none - - - - 409
/etc/udev/rules.d/80-installer-audio-power.rules

# Audio power saving only on battery, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings: on the charger it makes some laptops crackle.
ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="sound", KERNEL=="card*", DRIVERS=="snd_hda_intel", RUN+="/usr/local/libexec/installer-audio-power"
ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="power_supply", ENV{POWER_SUPPLY_TYPE}=="Mains", RUN+="/usr/local/libexec/installer-audio-power"
/usr/local/libexec/installer-audio-power

#!/bin/sh
# Audio power saving only on battery, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings.
# udev runs this when the sound card appears and when the charger is plugged in or out (/etc/udev/rules.d/80-installer-audio-power.rules).
param=/sys/module/snd_hda_intel/parameters/power_save
[ -w "$param" ] || exit 0
mains=0
online=0
for supply in /sys/class/power_supply/*; do
	[ "$(cat "$supply/type" 2>/dev/null)" = Mains ] || continue
	mains=1
	[ "$(cat "$supply/online" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && online=1
done
if [ "$mains" = 1 ] && [ "$online" = 0 ]; then
	echo 1 > "$param"
else
	echo 0 > "$param"
fi
exit 0
/etc/modprobe.d/installer-watchdog.conf

# Watchdog timers, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings: a desktop or laptop does not use them, and without them it starts and stops a little faster.
# Delete this file to load them again.
blacklist iTCO_wdt
blacklist sp5100_tco
blacklist wdat_wdt
first_steps: Razer devices: open RazerGenie to choose colours and DPI. You were added to the group plugdev; log out and in once so it applies.
notes: OpenRazer is built on this PC against your kernel; a kernel update rebuilds it. If the build fails the system still starts without it.
post_steps: if [ -f /usr/share/openrazer/openrazer-daemon.desktop ]; then mkdir -p /etc/xdg/autostart && ln -sf /usr/share/openrazer/openrazer-daemon.desktop /etc/xdg/autostart/openrazer-daemon.desktop; fi; exit 0
if getent group pipewire >/dev/null; then usermod -aG pipewire "$1"; fi; exit 0
